tokio.name: tokio
tokio.notes: Rust async runtime. Base = master HEAD 2026-11-17 (1f5eac54, tokio 1.54.1, tokio-util 0.7.20). Cargo workspace (resolver 2, edition 2021, rust-version 1.85, CI on stable; image uses rustc 1.98.0): tokio (runtime: scheduler current_thread + multi_thread, task/ = raw task state, harness, JoinHandle, AbortHandle, JoinSet, LocalSet, task-locals; sync/ = Notify, batch_semaphore behind Semaphore/Mutex/RwLock, mpsc bounded+unbounded over mpsc/{list,block,chan}.rs, broadcast, watch, oneshot, OnceCell, SetOnce, Barrier; time/ = timer wheel, sleep, timeout, interval, paused clock; io/, net/, fs/, process/, signal/; macros select!/join!/try_join!; coop budget), tokio-macros, tokio-test (task::spawn gives a future/stream you poll by hand with a mock waker: .poll(), .is_woken(), .waker_ref_count(); assert_pending!/assert_ready!/assert_ready_ok!/assert_ready_eq!), tokio-stream (wrappers: BroadcastStream, WatchStream, ReceiverStream, StreamMap, ...), tokio-util (sync/: CancellationToken with tree_node.rs parent/child tree + guard + WaitForCancellationFuture(Owned) + run_until_cancelled, PollSender in sync/mpsc.rs, PollSemaphore, ReusableBoxFuture; task/: TaskTracker, JoinMap, JoinQueue, AbortOnDropHandle, spawn_pinned LocalPoolHandle; time/: DelayQueue; codec, io, compat, udp), plus internal crates benches, examples, stress-test, tests-build, tests-integration (do not use). A root [patch.crates-io] points every workspace crate at its path. THERE IS NO Cargo.lock IN THE REPO (git-ignored, with target/ and .cargo/config*): the task must ship ONE generated lockfile and build with --locked, or every image rebuild resolves different dependency versions. TESTS: integration tests are one file = one test binary, auto-discovered (no autotests switch, no [[test]] tables in tokio or tokio-util), so a NEW file tokio/tests/<name>.rs or tokio-util/tests/<name>.rs needs NO edit to any existing file. tokio/tests has 190 files (sync_*.rs, task_*.rs, rt_*.rs, time_*.rs, macros_select.rs, ...), each starting with `#![warn(rust_2018_idioms)]` and `#![cfg(feature = "full")]` (or a narrower feature); tokio-util/tests has 31 (sync_cancellation_token.rs, task_tracker.rs, task_join_map.rs, task_join_queue.rs, mpsc.rs = PollSender, poll_semaphore.rs, time_delay_queue.rs, ...). Unit tests live in src (tokio --lib: 173 tests). Run from /app: `cargo test --locked --offline -p tokio --features full,test-util --test <file> -- --exact <name>...` and `cargo test --locked --offline -p tokio-util --features full --test <file> -- --exact <name>...` (CI feature set is full,test-util). Deterministic tools: tokio_test::task::spawn + manual poll; `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` / tokio::time::pause + advance on a current_thread runtime (time only moves when the runtime is idle or on advance); tokio::task::yield_now ordering on current_thread; dropping a future between two polls to model cancellation; counting wakes with is_woken(); Arc strong counts and Drop probes to detect leaks. LOOM IS NOT USABLE for hidden tests: loom tests are modules registered in existing files (tokio/src/sync/tests/mod.rs lists loom_notify, loom_mpsc, ...; tokio-util/src/sync/tests/mod.rs), so a new loom test needs an edit to an existing file, which the gate forbids for test.patch; the loom build is also not warmed in the image (a `--cfg loom` release build failed offline in the prototype). MEASURED 2026-11-17 offline (--network none; prototype factory/work/tmp/run10/tokio-proto/Dockerfile + smoke.sh; 8 CPUs, 8 GB Docker VM, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0, CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=line-tables-only): cold image build 766 s (base image pull ~9 min, generate-lockfile + cargo fetch 8 s, warm tokio full,test-util --no-run 91 s, tokio-util 17 s, tokio-test + tokio-stream 7 s), image 6.4 GB, target/ 3.0 GB, registry 189 MB. 8 sync_* test files 7 s (all pass), task_abort/task_join_set/task_local_set/rt_common/rt_threaded/rt_basic/macros_select/time_pause 6 s, tokio --lib 3 s, whole tokio-util 21 s, tokio-test + tokio-stream 5 s. A NEW test file compiles and runs in ~1 s. After an edit to tokio/src: the named test targets rebuild in ~7 s; relinking ALL 190 tokio test binaries takes 70 s and peaks at 2.1 GB (so never build all targets in test.sh; name the targets); tokio-util after a tokio edit 18 s. git status stays clean. No AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md in the repo. AVOID: tests-integration, tests-build, stress-test, benches, examples; anything needing tokio_unstable (--cfg tokio_unstable: tracing, io-uring, runtime metrics, task dumps), loom, miri, wasm, nextest (not installed); net/process/signal/fs tests as F2P (real OS resources); multi_thread runtime tests whose result depends on thread scheduling; real time (sleep without paused time, Instant::now timing). TARGET (painpoints.md): PP-16 (interleaving-dependent, state shared across wakers/permits/tasks), PP-17 (first plausible cause is one of several places), PP-07 (state over time: poll, cancel, re-poll, close), PP-10 (guards on nearby documented behavior: FIFO fairness, close semantics, cancel safety).
build_rules: Dockerfile: base rust:1.98.0-bookworm (rust-version 1.85, CI uses stable; check `rustc --version` in the image). apt: git ca-certificates. git init/fetch the base commit as usual and remove origin. `ENV CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=line-tables-only CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never` BEFORE warming (other values change the cache key; jobs=4 because Docker has 8 GB: measured peak 2.1 GB when relinking all tokio test binaries). LOCKFILE: the repo has no Cargo.lock (git-ignored). Generate it ONCE (`cargo generate-lockfile` in a scratch container, or copy /app/Cargo.lock out of the prototype image run10-tokio-proto), save it as environment/Cargo.lock, `COPY Cargo.lock /app/Cargo.lock` in the Dockerfile, then `cargo fetch --locked`. Never run generate-lockfile in the Dockerfile. Warm exactly what test.sh runs: `cargo test --locked -p tokio --features full,test-util --no-run`, `cargo test --locked -p tokio-util --features full --no-run`, and `cargo test --locked -p tokio-test -p tokio-stream --all-features --no-run` only if those crates are tested. Then `ENV CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true`. Confirm `git status --porcelain` is empty (Cargo.lock and target/ are ignored). Prototype: factory/work/tmp/run10/tokio-proto/Dockerfile (cold build 766 s incl. ~9 min base pull, image 6.4 GB).

Record in the build report: image size, cold image build time, the time of one verifier run on the oracle, and peak memory if you measured it (`cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.peak` inside the container). If a link step is killed for memory, lower CARGO_BUILD_JOBS (2), never raise it. task.toml: memory_mb 8192, cpus 4, storage_mb >= 20480; verifier timeout >= 1800 s; build_timeout_sec >= 3600.

Hidden tests: NEW integration test files only (tokio/tests/<name>.rs, tokio-util/tests/<name>.rs, tokio-stream/tests/<name>.rs): Cargo discovers them without editing any existing file. No loom, no src/ unit-test modules (they need an existing mod.rs edited), no tokio_unstable, no nextest, no net/process/signal/fs resources. Start each file like its neighbors (`#![warn(rust_2018_idioms)]`, `#![cfg(feature = "full")]` in tokio/tests). Use only public API that exists at base; pick file and test names that do not collide with existing ones (grep). Force every interleaving by hand: tokio_test::task::spawn + poll with assert_pending!/assert_ready!, is_woken(), dropping a future between two polls, and current_thread runtimes with paused time (`#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]`) when a runtime is needed. Never sleeps as synchronization, real time, multi_thread scheduling luck, or repeat-until-it-shows loops. FEATURE TASK EXCEPTION: when the F2P tests call API the task adds, their file fails to COMPILE at base; that is the expected base failure. Then keep F2P tests in their own new file(s) and every guard in SEPARATE new file(s) that use only base API (guards must compile and pass at base), and prove the assertions bite by running each trap implementation from the proposal through the verifier (each must fail a named F2P test on an assertion). Otherwise each F2P test must fail at base on an ASSERTION every time. In all cases never by hanging or timing out (assert a stuck future with assert_pending!/is_woken on a hand-polled future; put a hard `tokio::time::timeout` under paused time around anything that awaits).

test.sh: restore every verifier input from the pinned base (the existing files under tokio/tests, tokio-util/tests, tokio-stream/tests, tokio-test/, every Cargo.toml in the workspace, and /app/Cargo.lock from a copy kept outside /app, e.g. /opt/verifier/Cargo.lock written at image build); delete test files the base doesn't have in those dirs; apply test.patch. Then from /app, one invocation per group with EXACT names: `cargo test --locked --offline -p <crate> --features <same as warmed> --test <file> -- --exact <name1> <name2> ...` for the F2P group, the new guard group, then the PASS_TO_PASS group = NAMED existing test targets in the touched area (`--test sync_mpsc --test sync_notify ...`, explicit list) plus `--lib` of the touched crate. For every group parse the `test result:` lines and compare passed counts with the expected number; FAIL CLOSED when a group selects zero tests, when the count differs, or when the build fails. Never build all 190 tokio test targets in test.sh (70 s and 2.1 GB after a source edit): name the targets.
PASS_TO_PASS: every existing test target used must pass 3/3 at BASE in the image, offline, before it goes into test.sh; drop any that fails even once and say so in the report.

Determinism check before finishing (REQUIRED, numbers in the build report): run the F2P + guard groups 5 times in a row on the oracle, plus once with a single-threaded harness (`-- --test-threads=1` added to the same exact-name invocations); also run the F2P group 5 times at BASE and confirm every F2P test fails every time on its assertion (not a hang, not a compile error); for a FEATURE task the base run is instead: the F2P file fails to compile at base 5/5, the guard files pass at base 5/5, and each trap implementation fails its named F2P test on an assertion. Any oracle failure or any base pass means the interleaving is not forced: fix the test, never add a retry or a sleep.

Reference fix: if the reviewer or the plan names a 'simpler correct fix', BUILD it and run it through the existing tests of the touched crates and the hidden tests before trusting it; report the result (the etcd lesson: the reviewer's 2-file fix failed 3 existing tests). Run each trap variant from the proposal through the verifier and report its reward.
Upstream moves daily: run the AP-6 upstream check on the fix files and search the repo's open and closed issues/PRs you can reach for the symptom; state in the report what could not be checked.

grpc-go.name: grpc-go
grpc-go.notes: Go gRPC implementation (module google.golang.org/grpc at the repo root; go.mod: go 1.26.0, no toolchain line; upstream CI tests on Go 1.26 and 1.27 with `go test -cpu 1,4 -timeout 7m ./...`; the image has go1.27.4). Base = master HEAD on 2026-11-17 (f8bb66bd, committed 2026-11-13). Ten nested modules exist (examples, interop, security, gcp, cmd, ...): stay in the root module. CLIENT CONNECTION LIFECYCLE (root package grpc): clientconn.go (ClientConn: NewClient/Dial, Connect, Close, enterIdleMode/exitIdleMode, updateResolverStateAndUnlock, connectivity state manager, addrConn = subchannel: connect/resetTransport/tearDown/updateConnectivityState), internal/idle (idle Manager: activity counting OnCallBegin/OnCallEnd, idle timer, tryEnterIdleMode, ExitIdleMode), resolver_wrapper.go (ccResolverWrapper between the resolver and the channel), balancer_wrapper.go (ccBalancerWrapper + acBalancerWrapper: serializer for balancer calls, NewSubConn, UpdateState, subchannel state listeners, producers, health listener), internal/balancer/gracefulswitch (LB policy switch), picker_wrapper.go (pickerWrapper: blocking pick, picker generations, updatePicker/reset/close), stream.go + call.go (newClientStream, retries, pick + transport attempt), internal/grpcsync (CallbackSerializer, Event, PubSub), internal/transport (http2 client/server, controlbuf, GOAWAY, keepalive), balancer/pickfirst (default policy; leaf of most trees), balancer/roundrobin, balancer/endpointsharding, service_config.go, internal/resolver (config selector, delegating resolver, dns, passthrough, unix). TESTS: every package uses the grpctest harness (`type s struct{ grpctest.Tester }`, `func Test(t *testing.T) { grpctest.RunSubTests(t, s{}) }`, test methods `func (s) TestXxx(t *testing.T)`); its teardown runs LEAK CHECKS (goroutines, timers, tracked buffers): a hidden test that leaves a ClientConn, server, stream or goroutine open FAILS, so close everything (defer cc.Close(), cancel contexts, drain streams). A new test file in an existing package just adds `func (s) Test...` methods; a NEW package needs its own `s` type + Test entry point. There is no TestMain anywhere. Unit tests of unexported lifecycle code: package grpc tests in the root (clientconn_test.go, picker_wrapper_test.go, balancer_wrapper_test.go, resolver_test.go, *_ext_test.go are package grpc_test). End-to-end lifecycle tests: internal/idle/idle_e2e_test.go (package idle_test: real channel + stubserver + manual resolver; idle timeout via grpc.WithIdleTimeout; internal.EnterIdleModeForTesting / ExitIdleModeForTesting hooks through the internal package), test/ (package test: clientconn_state_transition_test.go, balancer_switching_test.go, resolver_update_test.go, goaway_test.go, gracefulstop_test.go, subconn_test.go, clientconn_test.go, idleness-related tests), balancer/pickfirst tests. HELPERS that exist at base: resolver/manual (manual.NewBuilderWithScheme, r.UpdateState, r.InitialState, BuildCallback/ResolveNowCallback/CloseCallback hooks), internal/stubserver (StartTestService, StubServer with EmptyCallF/FullDuplexCallF), test/bufconn (in-memory listener + dialer), internal/testutils (NewChannel for step signalling, AwaitState/AwaitNoStateChange, RestartableListener, LocalTCPListener on 127.0.0.1:0, BlockingDialer, PipeListener, StateChanges), internal/balancer/stub (stub.Register(name, stub.BalancerFuncs{...}) to build a test balancer whose UpdateClientConnState/UpdateState/ExitIdle/Close run test code at an exact step), balancer.Picker implemented by the test (a picker whose Pick blocks on a test channel), grpc.WithContextDialer (control connection establishment), grpc.WithDefaultServiceConfig, connectivity state via cc.GetState/WaitForStateChange, internal hooks registered in internal/internal.go. testing/synctest is available in this Go version but the channel does real network I/O and uses its own timers through internal hooks: use it only for code with no real I/O in the bubble (bufconn pipes are channel-based; verify before relying on it). No gofail-style failpoints exist. MEASURED 2026-11-17 offline (--network none; prototype factory/work/tmp/run9/grpc-go-proto/Dockerfile + smoke.sh; cold image ~2 min: go mod download 7 s, go vet of . ./internal/... ./balancer/... ./resolver/... ./test/ 87 s): ALL PASS, `go test .` 11 s, ./internal/idle 14 s, ./internal/transport 13 s, ./balancer/... 16 s total (pickfirst 11 s), ./resolver/... 1 s, ./test/ 38 s (the whole end-to-end package), internal grpcsync/balancer/resolver/testutils/balancergroup 9 s; git status clean. Tests listen on 127.0.0.1:0 or bufconn (loopback works with --network none). AVOID: xds/ (large, slow, own e2e setup), interop/, examples/, benchmark/, security/ and the other nested modules, credentials that need real certificates beyond testdata/, the dns resolver against real DNS, binarylog, channelz as the target, tests that depend on real wall-clock backoff of seconds, anything behind build tags. No -race (CGO is off), so tests assert on OUTCOMES (RPC status, connectivity states seen, number of resolver/balancer builds and closes, picks served, goroutine/subchannel counts through existing hooks), never on the race detector. No AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md in the repo. TARGET (painpoints.md): PP-16 (interleaving-dependent, state shared across components), PP-07 (state over time: idle -> active -> idle, close during update), PP-17 (the first plausible cause is one of several places), PP-10 (guards on nearby behavior).
build_rules: Dockerfile: base golang:1.27-bookworm (go.mod needs go >= 1.26.0 and names no toolchain; upstream CI uses 1.26 and 1.27; check `go version` in the image). git init/fetch the base commit as usual and remove origin. `ENV CGO_ENABLED=0` BEFORE warming (a different value changes the cache key). `go mod download` (7 s), then warm with `go vet <packages the task touches + the P2P packages>` from /app (e.g. `go vet . ./internal/idle/... ./internal/transport/... ./balancer/pickfirst/... ./resolver/... ./test/`) and `go test -count=1 -run '^$' <same packages>` to link the test binaries. In the SAME RUN layer finish with `find "$(go env GOCACHE)" -type f -exec touch -m -d '2099-01-01T00:00:00Z' {} +` (intel.md: otherwise Go refreshes cache mtimes and overlayfs copies the cache on every verifier run). Then `ENV GOPROXY=off GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly` so agent and verifier are offline. Prototype: factory/work/tmp/run9/grpc-go-proto/Dockerfile.

Never use -race, build tags, `make`, scripts/vet.sh, the nested modules (examples, interop, security, gcp, cmd) or xds/. Hidden tests run offline with `--network none`: bufconn or 127.0.0.1:0 listeners only, no fixed ports, no real DNS, no shared dirs.

Hidden tests: NEW `*_test.go` files only, in existing packages (root package grpc for unexported lifecycle code, internal/idle, test/, balancer/pickfirst) or a new package with its own grpctest entry point (`type s struct{ grpctest.Tester }` + `func Test(t *testing.T) { grpctest.RunSubTests(t, s{}) }`); in existing packages add `func (s) TestXxx` methods and grep the package's _test.go files for name collisions (helper types and funcs too). Use only identifiers that exist at base. The harness leak-checks goroutines and timers at teardown: close every ClientConn, server, stream and context. The interleaving must be FORCED (test balancer via internal/balancer/stub, a test picker, manual resolver callbacks, a context dialer, wrappers that perform the racing action synchronously at an exact step, or testing/synctest), never hoped for with sleeps, GOMAXPROCS tricks or retry loops; no timing assertions. Each F2P test must fail at base on an assertion about the outcome every time; a hang is detected with a bounded wait for a specific expected event and reported through the assertion, never by the go test timeout or a panic.

test.sh: restore every verifier input from the pinned base (all existing *_test.go files in the tested packages, internal/grpctest, internal/leakcheck, internal/testutils, internal/stubserver, internal/balancer/stub, resolver/manual, test/bufconn, testdata, go.mod, go.sum); delete *_test.go files the base doesn't have in those packages; apply test.patch; then from /app `go test -count=1 -v -timeout 10m <pkg> -run '^Test$/^(exact F2P method names)$'` (grpctest runs methods as subtests of Test: check the exact -run form in the image and count the `--- PASS`/`--- FAIL` lines so a filter that matches nothing cannot pass), then the new guards, then NAMED existing tests as PASS_TO_PASS (an explicit list in the touched area) plus whole small packages where they are fast and stable; finally `go vet` of the touched packages. Each group is a separate invocation with an expected-pass count check.

PASS_TO_PASS admission (REQUIRED): every existing test or package used as PASS_TO_PASS must pass 3/3 at BASE in the image, offline, before it goes into test.sh; drop any that fails or is timing-sensitive, and list what was dropped in the build report (the etcd run had two existing tests that fail at base in this environment).

Determinism check before finishing (REQUIRED, report the numbers in the build report): run the F2P + guard groups 5 times in a row on the oracle (`-count=1` each run) and once with `-cpu 1,4`; also run the F2P group 5 times at BASE and confirm every F2P test fails every time on its assertion. Any oracle failure or any base pass means the interleaving is not forced: fix the test, never add a retry or a sleep.

If the proposal or the reviewer names a 'simpler correct fix', build it as a variant and run the full verifier (existing tests included) on it before treating it as correct; report the result. Run each trap variant from the proposal through the full verifier and report its reward.
Upstream moves daily: run the AP-6 upstream check on the fix files; state in the report what could not be checked (the operator runs the gh issue/PR search).

etcd.name: etcd
etcd.notes: Go distributed key-value store (Raft). Base = main HEAD 2026-11-16 (b32ff8a1). MULTI-MODULE repo with a go.work (go 1.27, toolchain go1.27.4): api, client/pkg, pkg, client/v3, server, etcdutl, etcdctl, cache, tests (+ tools). Go commands work from the repo ROOT through go.work (`cd /app && go test ./server/storage/mvcc/ ./tests/integration/`; verified offline) or from inside a module dir. Components: server/storage/mvcc (kvstore + treeIndex/keyIndex revisions, compaction in kvstore_compaction.go, watchableStore with synced/unsynced watcher groups + victims, syncWatchersLoop/syncVictimsLoop, watcher/WatchStream, Restore), server/storage/backend (bbolt batch tx, read tx buffers), server/storage/schema, server/storage/wal, server/lease (lessor: Grant/Revoke/Renew/Checkpoint/Promote/Demote/Recover, expiry heap lease_queue, RangeDeleter into mvcc, Checkpointer through raft; leasehttp forwards renew to the leader), server/etcdserver (raft loop raft.go, apply path server.go + apply/, v3_server.go linearizable reads + lease RPC entry points, snapshot/restore, api/v3rpc gRPC incl. watch.go serverWatchStream, txn/), server/auth, client/v3 (watch.go watchGrpcStream resumption after a stream break, lease.go keepalive loops, retry interceptor, concurrency/ locks+elections, leasing/, ordering/, namespace/, mirror/), cache/ (client-side watch cache; its tests already use testing/synctest), pkg/. TESTS: unit tests live next to the code (testify; mvcc tests build a store on a temp bbolt backend via betesting.NewDefaultTmpBackend(t) and lease.FakeLessor or a real lessor; lessor tests use NewTestBackend + newLessor with a fake cluster). In-process cluster tests: tests/integration (package integration) and tests/integration/clientv3/{lease,watch,concurrency,...} use tests/framework/integration: integration.BeforeTest(t) + integration.NewCluster(t, &integration.ClusterConfig{Size: N}) start real members IN THE TEST PROCESS over unix sockets (no fixed TCP ports; UseBridge puts a controllable bridge between client and server: bridge DropConnections/Blackhole/Unblackhole, used to break and resume client streams deterministically), members can be Stop/Restart-ed. Their TestMain is only goroutine-leak detection (testutil.MustTestMainWithLeakDetection): a hidden test that leaves a goroutine, client or cluster open FAILS the whole package, so close everything in t.Cleanup/defer clus.Terminate(t). GOFAIL FAILPOINTS ARE NOT USABLE: the `// gofail:` comments (54 in server/) only become code after `make gofail-enable` rewrites the sources (dirty tree, needs the gofail tool); without it gofail.List() is empty and failpoint tests skip (integration.SkipIfNoGoFail). Hidden tests must force interleavings another way: package-internal tests that drive the unexported step functions directly instead of the background loops (e.g. call syncWatchers / the victim sync / the lessor's expiry or checkpoint step by hand between operations), channels and hooks the code already exposes (watch response channels with chosen buffer sizes to create victims, the fake RangeDeleter/Checkpointer callbacks of the lessor, the bridge, member Stop/Restart, raft readiness via existing test helpers), or testing/synctest (stable in this Go version; only for code that does no real I/O inside the bubble: bbolt fsync and sockets are not durably blocking). MEASURED 2026-11-17 offline (--network none; prototype factory/work/tmp/run8/etcd-proto/Dockerfile + smoke.sh, image 4.9 GB, cold build ~4 min: go mod download of all modules 79 s, go vet of server storage/lease/etcdserver/auth + client/v3 + cache + tests integration/framework 74 s): server ./storage/mvcc/... 73 s, ./lease/... 10 s, storage backend+schema+wal 64 s, ./etcdserver/... 55 s, ./auth 2 s, client/v3 unit 3 s, cache 3 s; tests/integration single tests 1-3 s each (4 named tests 6 s); tests/integration/clientv3/lease whole package 215 s, clientv3/watch 180 s; git status clean. KNOWN BAD AT BASE in this environment, never use as PASS_TO_PASS: tests/integration/clientv3/watch TestV3WatchProgressWaitsForSync (fails 3/3: 1001 writes miss its 10 s deadline on this disk), server/storage/mvcc TestWatchRestore (failed once in the full package run, passed 4/4 alone: timing-sensitive). So P2P = NAMED tests, each checked 3x at base in the image, never whole integration packages. AVOID: tests/e2e and tests/robustness (start etcd binaries, need a built bin/ and failpoints), tests/antithesis, anything behind build tags (cluster_proxy, e2e), TLS cert generation scripts, `make` targets, tools/, proxy/grpcproxy as a target. No -race (CGO is off), so tests assert on OUTCOMES (events received, revisions, lease state), never on the race detector. No AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md in the repo. TARGET (painpoints.md): PP-16 (interleaving-dependent, state shared across components), PP-07 (state over time: restore, compaction, leader change), PP-17 (the first plausible cause is one of several places), PP-10 (guards on nearby behavior).

Use only identifiers that exist at base; grep the package's existing _test.go files for name collisions. In packages with the leak-detection TestMain, close every cluster, client, watcher, store and backend (t.Cleanup / defer). The interleaving must be FORCED (explicit channels/hooks, hand-driven steps, bridge, restart, or testing/synctest), never hoped for with sleeps, GOMAXPROCS tricks or retry loops; no timing assertions. Each F2P test must fail at base on an assertion about the outcome every time, not by deadlock/timeout/panic.

test.sh: restore every verifier input from the pinned base (all existing *_test.go files in the tested packages, tests/framework, client/pkg/testutil, server/storage/backend/testing, server/storage/mvcc/testutil, go.mod/go.sum/go.work/go.work.sum of every module); delete *_test.go files the base doesn't have in those packages; apply test.patch; then, from /app, `go test -count=1 -v -timeout 10m <pkg> -run '^(exact F2P names)$'`, then the new guards, then NAMED existing tests as PASS_TO_PASS (`-run '^(A|B|C)$'`, an explicit list in the touched area, each verified 3x at base in the image; never a whole integration package, never TestV3WatchProgressWaitsForSync or TestWatchRestore); finally `go vet` of the touched packages. Each group is a separate invocation with an expected-pass count check.

Determinism check before finishing (REQUIRED, report the numbers in the build report): run the F2P + guard groups 5 times in a row on the oracle (`-count=1` each run) and once with `-cpu 1,4`; also run the F2P group 5 times at BASE and confirm every F2P test fails every time on its assertion. Any oracle failure or any base pass means the interleaving is not forced: fix the test, never add a retry or a sleep.
Upstream moves daily: run the AP-6 upstream check on the fix files and search the repo's open issues/PRs text you can reach for the symptom; state in the report what could not be checked.

harbor.name: harbor
harbor.notes: Go module under src/. Many packages need PostgreSQL via TestMain; hidden tests must live in DB-free packages. See intel.md 'DB-backed' notes. Swagger-generated code is not committed: never use 'go build ./...'.
build_rules: Warm caches in the Dockerfile with `go mod download` + `go vet <packages>` (vet compiles tests without running TestMain); `go test -run '^$'` only on DB-free packages.
After warming: `ENV GOPROXY=off GOTOOLCHAIN=local` so agent/verifier are offline.
Never `go build ./...` (swagger-generated code is not committed).
Hidden tests: NEW `*_test.go` files only, in packages without a DB TestMain (grep the package's _test.go files for TestMain / PrepareTestForPostgresSQL).
test.sh: `go test -count=1 -v <pkg> -run '^(...)$'` for F2P and guards, whole DB-free packages for P2P, then `go vet` of dependent packages.

hoppscotch.name: hoppscotch
hoppscotch.notes: TypeScript pnpm monorepo (packageManager pnpm@10.34.5, node >= 22), base = release 2026.10.1. Test suites: packages/hoppscotch-common (vitest, ~94 spec files: helpers, services, kernel logic, request/collection handling), packages/hoppscotch-js-sandbox (vitest, ~80: pre-request/test script sandbox, pw/hopp APIs), packages/hoppscotch-backend (jest, NestJS, ~19 unit specs; verify they mock Prisma and need no DB), packages/hoppscotch-data (schemas/migrations of collections and requests). AVOID packages/hoppscotch-cli tests (they build the CLI and some need a running backend/network) and Vue component rendering. Hidden tests must run offline with node_modules installed in the image at build time (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile), run with the package's own runner (vitest run / jest) by file path.
build_rules: Toolchain: `corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@10.34.5 --activate` (version from package.json packageManager); node from the base image.

Dockerfile: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` at build time, then build ONLY the workspace packages the tested package imports through their built output (check the tested package's vitest/tsconfig aliases and each dependency's package.json main/exports; e.g. @hoppscotch/data, @hoppscotch/js-sandbox if resolved from dist). Run the chosen spec files once at build time so caches are warm. Then set `ENV npm_config_offline=true` (and do not need the network afterwards).
Large monorepo: keep the image build deterministic; don't run the whole repo's build or test suites.

Hidden tests: NEW `*.spec.ts` files next to the existing specs of the same area (same vitest config picks them up). Mock with `vi.mock` only at module boundaries that exist at the base commit; never import new helper names from the fix.

test.sh: `cd /app/packages/<pkg> && pnpm exec vitest run <explicit spec files>` (or `pnpm exec jest <files>` for the backend), F2P and guards as separate invocations so the log shows which group failed; then `pnpm exec vue-tsc --noEmit` or `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p <tsconfig>` for the package ONLY if it passes at base in the image (check first; skip if base already has type errors).
A hidden-test file that fails at base must fail on assertions, not on module resolution or type errors.

sqlglot.name: sqlglot
sqlglot.notes: Pure-Python SQL parser/transpiler/optimizer/executor, 31+ dialects (sqlglot/dialects/*.py subclass Dialect with Tokenizer/Parser/Generator inner classes; sqlglot/expressions, parser.py, generator.py, optimizer/*, executor/*, transforms.py). Tests: stdlib unittest, ~58 files: tests/test_*.py and tests/dialects/test_<dialect>.py (validate_identity / validate_all helpers in tests/dialects/test_dialect.py), plus SQL fixtures under tests/fixtures (optimizer/*.sql, identity.sql, pretty.sql). ALL unit tests are offline. Only tests/test_executor.py and parts of tests/test_optimizer.py import duckdb/pandas (in-process, no server), so install them at build time. SKIP_INTEGRATION=1 only skips the in-process duckdb TPC-H/TPC-DS comparisons in tests/test_executor.py (local fixtures, offline): leave it UNSET in the verifier, they are a good guard. AVOID: the sqlglot-integration-tests submodule (private git@ URL, absent in the image; nothing in tests/ needs it), the mypyc C extension (sqlglotc/, *.so) and benchmarks/. The repo has AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md that Codex will read; check they hold no hints for the chosen defect. sqlglot ships very fast upstream (several commits/day): run the AP-6 upstream check carefully and prefer cross-dialect contracts (parse in dialect A, generate in B, optimizer + dialect interplay) over single-dialect syntax gaps (those are AP-4 one-liners).
build_rules: Dockerfile: base python:3.12-slim-bookworm + `apt-get install -y git`; git init/fetch the base commit as usual; then `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=0.0.0 pip install --no-cache-dir -e . duckdb pandas python-dateutil pytz typing_extensions pytest` (do NOT install the [c]/sqlglotc extra). sqlglot/_version.py is git-ignored, so the tree stays clean; confirm `git status --porcelain` is empty.

Warm and check at build time: `python -m unittest tests.test_parser tests.dialects.test_dialect tests.test_executor` must pass. Then `ENV PIP_NO_INDEX=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` so agent/verifier are offline and no __pycache__ dirties the tree.

Hidden tests: NEW files `tests/test_<topic>_hidden.py` or `tests/dialects/test_<dialect>_<topic>.py` (unittest.TestCase classes; may import tests.dialects.test_dialect.Validator and tests.helpers). Test through public API only: sqlglot.parse_one/transpile/exp builders, sqlglot.optimizer.optimize, sqlglot.executor.execute, Dialect.get_or_raise. Never import names that only the fix adds. New SQL fixture files under tests/fixtures are allowed (new files only).
Never edit existing tests/fixtures files in test.patch (gate forbids modifying existing test files); if a fixture must change, put the expectation in the new test file instead.

test.sh: `cd /app && python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider <explicit new test files>` for F2P and guards (separate invocations), then P2P = explicit existing modules, e.g. `python -m unittest tests.test_transpile tests.dialects.test_<dialect> ...` (always include every dialect test module the fix touches plus tests.test_optimizer and tests.test_parser). Restore every verifier input (tests/helpers.py, tests/dialects/test_dialect.py, existing fixtures, setup.cfg/pyproject) from the base commit before running.

pdal.name: pdal
pdal.notes: C++17 point-cloud library: core in pdal/ (PointTable/PointView/PointLayout, Stage, StageFactory, PipelineManager/PipelineReaderJSON, Options, SpatialReference, expression/Where), readers/writers in io/, filters in filters/, kernels (pdal info/translate/pipeline CLI) in kernels/, apps/. Plugins (plugins/*: arrow, tiledb, hdf, draco, e57, pgpointcloud, nitf, ...) need extra deps: AVOID them. Tests: GoogleTest executables registered with PDAL_ADD_TEST in test/unit/CMakeLists.txt (one executable per *Test.cpp, run via ctest or the binary in build/bin). Test data in test/data (committed). Offline and hermetic: most test/unit/*Test.cpp and test/unit/filters/*, io tests for LAS/LAZ (lazperf vendored), BPF, PLY, PCD, text, faux, OBJ, SBET, COPC (local files), pipeline/kernel tests. AVOID network tests: io/CopcRemoteReaderTest, io/StacReaderTest, io/i3s*, anything using http(s) URLs or arbiter remote I/O, and pgpointcloud. Required deps: GDAL (+PROJ), GeoTIFF, curl, zlib, zstd, lzma, libxml2; nlohmann/eigen/lazperf/h3/utfcpp are vendored.
build_rules: Dockerfile, deps layer FIRST (cache it; it does not depend on the source): base condaforge/miniforge3:26.9.4-2, `mamba create -y -n pdal -c conda-forge compilers cmake ninja libgdal-core geotiff gtest libcurl zlib zstd xz libxml2 git && conda clean -afy`. Use `SHELL ["conda", "run", "-n", "pdal", "/bin/bash", "-c"]` or set PATH/CONDA_PREFIX explicitly so cmake finds the env.

Then fetch the base commit into /app as usual and configure ONLY the core: `cmake -S /app -B /app/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DWITH_TESTS=ON -DUSE_EXTERNAL_GTEST=ON -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=$CONDA_PREFIX` with every BUILD_PLUGIN_* OFF (default). /build* is already in PDAL's .gitignore; confirm `git status --porcelain` stays empty.

Build only what the tests need: `ninja -C /app/build pdalcpp <the F2P/P2P test targets> pdal` (names from PDAL_ADD_TEST, e.g. pdal_filters_crop_test). Don't build every test executable: a full build is ~150 targets. Expect 15-30 min for the image; keep it under 50 min. Ninja makes incremental rebuilds in the verifier fast.

Hidden tests: NEW `test/unit/**/<Name>Test.cpp` files (+ new data files under test/data if needed). Registering them requires adding PDAL_ADD_TEST lines to test/unit/CMakeLists.txt; that is the ONE existing file test.patch may modify (the gate allows it for cpp). Use only APIs that exist at base (public headers in pdal/, io/, filters/; Options, StageFactory, PipelineManager, PointTable/PointView); never a class/method only the fix adds.

test.sh: restore test/unit/CMakeLists.txt, test/unit/Support.*, TestConfig.hpp.in and any test data the tests read from the base commit, apply test.patch, re-run cmake (same flags, offline), `ninja -C /app/build <targets>`; then run each test binary from /app/build with `--gtest_filter` for F2P/guards and whole P2P binaries (explicit list). A build/compile failure gives reward 0. Use `ctest --test-dir /app/build -R '^(name1|name2)$' --output-on-failure` or the binaries directly; set PDAL_DRIVER_PATH=/app/build/lib.
Offline: after the build `ENV CONDA_OFFLINE=1`; nothing in test.sh may download.

typst.name: typst
typst.notes: Rust workspace (Cargo.lock, rust-version 1.92, CI on 1.98.0), ~17 crates: typst-syntax (lexer/parser), typst-eval (interpreter), typst-library (std library: foundations, model, layout, text, math, introspection, visualize), typst-realize (show rules), typst-layout, typst-html, typst-pdf, typst-svg, typst-render, typst-ide (autocomplete/tooltips), typst-cli. Tests are all offline: the integration suite tests/suite/**/*.typ (sections `--- name attrs ---`, with `#test(a, b)` / `#assert` and `// Error:` / `// Warning:` annotations; output compared to tests/ref/ files or hashed refs in tests/ref/<format>/hashes.txt), run by `cargo test --workspace --test tests -- <filters>`, plus Rust unit tests inside crates (`cargo test -p <crate>`). Fonts and assets come from pinned git dependencies (typst-assets, typst-dev-assets), fetched once at image build. AVOID: typst-cli network features (package downloads from packages.typst.org), tests/packages that need a registry, fuzz/, docs generation. Prefer cross-crate contracts: eval + realize + layout, paged vs HTML targets (same document must behave consistently in both), syntax + IDE.
build_rules: Dockerfile: base rust:1.98.0-bookworm; git init/fetch the base commit; `cargo fetch --locked` (pulls crates.io and the pinned git deps), then `cargo test --workspace --test tests --no-run --locked` and `cargo test -p <crates the task touches> --no-run --locked` to warm target/. Then `ENV CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true`. target/ and tests/store/ are git-ignored; confirm `git status --porcelain` is empty.
Expect 10-20 min and several GB for the image; give Docker at least 8 GB RAM; use `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4` if memory runs out.

Hidden tests: preferably NEW suite files `tests/suite/<area>/<topic>-hidden.typ` whose tests produce NO visual output and check behavior with `#test(...)`, `#assert`, `// Error:` / `// Warning:` annotations, or html-stage tests with NEW reference files under tests/ref/html/. Do NOT rely on hashed references (they would need edits to existing tests/ref/*/hashes.txt, which the gate forbids). Rust-level tests: NEW files `crates/<crate>/tests/<name>.rs` using only that crate's public API at base.

test.sh: restore tests/src, tests/Cargo.toml, tests/ref, .cargo/config.toml and Cargo.lock from the base commit; `cd /app && cargo test --offline --workspace --test tests -- --no-report <F2P test names, exact>` then guards, then P2P = the existing suite for the affected areas by path (`-p tests/suite/<area>`, explicit list) plus `cargo test --offline -p <touched crates>`. A test with output but no reference fails, so check every new test at base with the oracle.
Never use `cargo testit` in test.sh (it runs a wrapper that may try to regenerate artifacts by checking out other commits).

traefik.name: traefik
traefik.notes: Go reverse proxy (module github.com/traefik/traefik/v3, go 1.27.0, module at repo root). Request path: EntryPoint -> Router -> Middleware chain -> Service. Static config (pkg/config/static, startup) vs dynamic config (pkg/config/dynamic, produced by providers at runtime). Unit tests (testify, table-driven) under pkg/ and cmd/: providers with fake clients and fixture files (pkg/provider/kubernetes/{crd,ingress,gateway,knative} use fake clientsets + YAML fixtures; docker, consulcatalog, nomad, ecs, kv, file, http, rest, acme), the configuration watcher/aggregator and router/service/middleware builders (pkg/server, pkg/server/router, pkg/server/service), middlewares (pkg/middlewares/*), TLS store/manager (pkg/tls), muxer/rules (pkg/muxer), tcp/udp. AVOID integration/ (needs Docker and real services); pkg/middlewares/requestdecorator (tests resolve real DNS CNAMEs, fail offline) and pkg/middlewares/ratelimiter (Redis rate tests are timing-sensitive, failed under load) as P2P; and anything that needs the webui build: webui/static only holds a placeholder that keeps the go:embed compiling; never run `make` targets (generate-webui uses Docker). The repo ships AGENTS.md (canonical agent guide, which Codex reads) and CLAUDE.md (pointer): check they hold no hints for the chosen defect. Prefer contracts that cross packages: provider -> dynamic config merge/validation -> router/service build -> API/status output (pkg/api), or static config -> entrypoint/runtime behavior.
build_rules: Dockerfile: base golang:1.27-bookworm; git init/fetch the base commit as usual; `go mod download`, then warm the build cache with `go vet <packages the task touches and their dependents>` (vet compiles packages and tests without running them; `go vet ./pkg/... ./cmd/...` also works but takes longer), then run the chosen F2P/P2P packages once with `go test -count=1 -run '^$'`. Then `ENV GOPROXY=off GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly` so agent/verifier are offline.
Never `go build ./...` from the root without checking it works at base, and never `make` (generate-webui needs Docker).

Hidden tests: NEW `*_test.go` files in the packages under test (pkg/...), plus new fixture files under that package's existing fixtures/testdata dir if needed (new files only). Use only exported APIs and package-level seams that exist at base; avoid type/func names that collide with the package's existing _test.go files.

test.sh: `go test -count=1 -v ./pkg/<pkg>/ -run '^(...)$'` for F2P and guards (separate invocations), whole packages for P2P (explicit list), then `go vet` of the dependent packages. Restore every verifier input (existing _test.go files, fixtures, testdata, go.mod/go.sum) from the pinned base before running.
Every chosen package must pass `go test` with `--network none` at base (loopback only); check this at build time.

Measured 2026-11-14 (prototype factory/work/tmp/traefik-proto/Dockerfile): go mod download ~5 min, `go vet ./pkg/... ./cmd/...` ~16 min, image export ~21 min (huge build cache) = ~46 min cold; `go test ./pkg/... ./cmd/...` offline ~15 min. Vet ONLY the packages the task needs to keep the image small and the build well under an hour.

apisix.name: apisix
apisix.notes: Lua/OpenResty API gateway. Core in apisix/ (init.lua request phases, http/router/ + router.lua (radixtree uri/host), http/route.lua, upstream.lua + balancer/ (roundrobin, chash, ewma, least_conn, priority), healthcheck manager, admin/ (Admin API + schema validation), core/ (config_etcd / config_yaml watchers, schema, ctx/vars, table utils), plugin.lua (plugin loading, merging route/service/consumer/global plugins, priority order, plugin_config), consumer.lua + auth plugins, ssl/ (SNI cert matching), stream/, control/ (control API), secret/ (secret refs), timers, slow_start.lua, healthcheck_manager.lua). Tests: Test::Nginx `.t` files under t/ (t/core, t/admin, t/router, t/node, t/plugin, t/config-center-yaml, ...) run with `prove -I/opt/test-nginx/lib -I./ <files>` from /app; t/APISIX.pm starts nginx with a generated config and talks to etcd at 127.0.0.1:2379 (config_provider etcd); the yaml config center (t/config-center-yaml) needs no etcd. Each test file starts its own nginx with test upstreams on 127.0.0.1:1980/1981/... (t/lib/server.lua). AVOID: anything that talks to external services (redis, kafka, keycloak, vault, consul/nacos/eureka/kubernetes discovery, cloud APIs, ldap, elasticsearch, clickhouse, opentelemetry/zipkin collectors, grpc/grpc-web/dubbo/sse example servers, wasm, xrpc, http3, coredns-based DNS tests) and tests that resolve public hostnames. The repo ships AGENTS.md (points to the security threat model).
build_rules: Dockerfile (mirrors upstream CI ci/linux_openresty_common_runner.sh): base debian:bookworm-slim; apt-get install ca-certificates wget curl git make gcc g++ build-essential cpanminus perl libpcre2-dev libyaml-dev libssl-dev libncurses5-dev libreadline-dev libxml2-dev libxslt-dev pkg-config zlib1g-dev file cmake unzip sudo procps (make deps compiles C rocks: lua-resty-saml builds xmlsec1 and needs libxml2-dev, zlib1g-dev and file; api7-lua-rapidjson needs cmake); install the apisix-runtime 1.4.2 .deb from github.com/api7/apisix-build-tools releases (apisix-runtime-debug_1.4.2-0.debianbookworm-slim_amd64.deb, sha256 0fdc2043... as in ci/linux-install-openresty.sh); PATH=/usr/local/openresty/nginx/sbin:/usr/local/openresty/luajit/bin:/usr/local/openresty/bin:$PATH; `cpanm --notest Test::Nginx`; test-nginx cloned to /opt/test-nginx at the commit pinned by upstream CI (ced30a31bafab6c68873efb17b6d80f39bcd95f5); etcd + etcdctl v3.5.4 binaries in /usr/local/bin. Then git init/fetch the base commit into /app AND check out the test submodule before removing origin: `git submodule update --init --depth 1 t/toolkit` (t/lib/test_admin.lua requires toolkit.json; without it every Admin-API test fails with 500). Then `bash utils/linux-install-luarocks.sh && make deps` (lua deps into /app/deps, git-ignored; confirm `git status --porcelain` is empty).

Warm and check at build time: start etcd, `make init`, run the chosen P2P .t files once with `prove`, stop etcd. Nothing may download afterwards: test.sh must not call luarocks, cpanm, wget or git fetch.

Hidden tests: NEW `t/**/*.t` files only (Test::Nginx blocks: --- config / --- request / --- response_body / --- error_log / --- no_error_log). They may use the test upstreams t/APISIX.pm already provides and Admin API calls through t/lib/test_admin.lua; never require a Lua module only the fix adds. Each F2P file must FAIL at base on a response/log assertion, not on a missing module or nginx start failure.

test.sh: restore t/APISIX.pm, t/lib/, t/certs/, conf/ and every existing .t file the run uses from the pinned base; append the /etc/hosts entries upstream CI adds (ci/common.sh set_coredns + build.yml: `127.0.0.1 test.com`, `127.0.0.1 admin.apisix.dev`, `127.0.1.1 httpbin.local`, `::1 ipv6.local`; Docker rewrites /etc/hosts at container start, so this must happen in test.sh, not the Dockerfile; without them t/node/upstream.t fails offline); start etcd ON 127.0.0.1 ONLY (`etcd --data-dir /tmp/etcd-data --listen-client-urls http://127.0.0.1:2379 --advertise-client-urls http://127.0.0.1:2379 --listen-peer-urls http://127.0.0.1:2380` in the background, wait until `etcdctl endpoint health` is OK), `cd /app && make init`, then `FLUSH_ETCD=1 prove -I/opt/test-nginx/lib -I./ <explicit F2P files>` then guards then P2P files (separate invocations); stop etcd and remove its data dir on every exit path (trap). Reward 1 only if every prove run passes.

A VERIFIED prototype (built and smoke-tested offline 2026-11-14: t/core/json.t, t/node/upstream.t, t/admin/routes.t, t/router/radixtree-uri-sanity.t = 256 tests PASS in 44 s, clean git status) is at factory/work/tmp/apisix-proto/Dockerfile + smoke.sh: start from it. Full cold image build ~25-30 min on this host (runtime .deb + cpanm Test::Nginx + make deps ~7 min + export ~3 min).
Timing: Test::Nginx files run sequentially and each block restarts nginx; keep the total verifier run under ~15 min.

nats.name: nats
nats.notes: Go message broker (module github.com/nats-io/nats-server/v2, go 1.26.0, toolchain go1.26.11, module at repo root). Almost everything is in the one big `server` package (~70 source files: client/parser/sublist core, accounts.go (imports/exports, service latency, subject mappings), subject_transform.go, auth*.go/jwt.go (permissions), route.go/gateway.go/leafnode.go (interest propagation between servers), JetStream: jetstream.go, jetstream_api.go (JSON API + error codes in jetstream_errors_generated.go), stream.go, consumer.go, filestore.go/memstore.go/store.go (storage + restart recovery), stream_backup.go, jetstream_batching.go, jetstream_cluster.go/raft.go (clustered; AVOID as test targets), mqtt.go and websocket.go (protocol layers over the core), monitor.go (/varz,/connz,/jsz HTTP), reload.go (config reload)). Tests: ~75 server/*_test.go files, run as `go test -count=1 -run '^TestX$' ./server`; CI splits by name prefix and build tags (scripts/runTestsOnTravis.sh: skip_js_cluster_tests*, skip_no_race_*). The only TestMain (server/sublist_test.go) just parses -cluster_compression/-leafnode_compression flags and seeds sublist benchmarks; no DB, no network. Helpers start in-process servers on 127.0.0.1: RunServer(&opts), RunServerWithConfig(createConfFile(t, ...)), RunBasicJetStreamServer(t) (Port -1, StoreDir t.TempDir()), checkFor(t, total, poll, func() error) for waiting, require_* assertion helpers (jetstream_helpers_test.go), nats.go client (nats.Connect(s.ClientURL())). WARNING: DefaultTestOptions has Port 4222 (fixed): hidden tests MUST set Port=-1 / `listen: 127.0.0.1:-1` and use t.TempDir() for store_dir. Measured 2026-11-14 (prototype factory/work/tmp/nats-proto/Dockerfile, offline): image ~2.5 min (go mod download ~15 s, `go vet ./server` 35 s, test-binary compile 58 s); one `go test -run '^TestX$' ./server` = 1.5-2.2 s warm (8 s first link); TestJetStreamAddStream, TestJetStreamConsumerMaxDeliveryAndServerRestart, TestFileStoreBasics, TestAccountImportsWithWildcardSupport, TestLeafNodeBasicAuthSingleton all pass with --network none. FLAKINESS is the main risk: TestJetStreamCluster*/TestJetStreamSuperCluster*/TestNRG*/TestNoRace* are timing-heavy multi-server tests: never use them as P2P and never build hidden tests on Raft clusters. Hidden tests: single server (or at most one server + one leafnode/gateway peer with checkFor-based sync), explicit restart via s.Shutdown() + RunServer with the same StoreDir, generous checkFor windows (>= 5 s), no time.Sleep as synchronization, no fixed ports, unique t.TempDir(). No -race (CGO disabled in the image). The repo ships AGENTS.md (Codex reads it): it tells agents to put tests in EXISTING test files and never create new ones; that only affects the solver, but test.sh must restore every existing *_test.go from base. Target areas (Sol weaknesses PP-07/PP-16 stateful + restart/recovery, PP-03 cross-component contracts, PP-11 implied cases, PP-02 indirect evidence): stream/consumer config -> validation -> filestore/memstore -> API responses and state after restart; subject mapping/transforms across accounts, imports/exports and permissions; leafnode interest propagation (single hub + leaf); MQTT/WebSocket session or retained state on top of JetStream; KV/object-store semantics via JetStream (TTL, history, purge, delete markers). Avoid external services, real clocks of minutes, and clusters.
build_rules: Dockerfile: base golang:1.26-bookworm (go.mod: go 1.26.0, toolchain go1.26.11; the image's toolchain must satisfy it, check `go version` >= 1.26.11 or keep GOTOOLCHAIN=local only after confirming). git init/fetch the base commit as usual, remove origin, `go mod download`, then warm the caches: `go vet ./server` (compiles package + tests, runs nothing; ~35 s) and `go test -count=1 -run '^$' ./server` (links the test binary; ~60 s; TestMain is harmless). Then `ENV GOPROXY=off GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly`. A working prototype is factory/work/tmp/nats-proto/Dockerfile.

Hidden tests: NEW `server/<topic>_hidden_test.go` files (package server) using only helpers and exported/unexported APIs that exist at base (RunServer, RunBasicJetStreamServer, createConfFile, checkFor, require_*, nats.go client). Avoid type/func names that collide with the ~75 existing test files (grep before naming). spicedb.name: spicedb
spicedb.notes: Go authorization database (Zanzibar-style; module github.com/authzed/spicedb, go 1.26.10, module at repo root; upstream builds with golang 1.27.3). Path of a permission question: schema text -> pkg/schemadsl (lexer/parser/compiler) -> pkg/schema + pkg/schema/v2 (type system, validation, reachability) and internal/namespace -> stored through pkg/datalayer over a datastore -> evaluated by internal/graph (check, expand, lookupresources2/3, lookupsubjects) through internal/dispatch (graph, caching, singleflight, keys) or by the newer plan-based evaluator pkg/query (iterator tree: arrow, union, intersection, exclusion, caveat, recursive; enabled per API via the experimental query-plan options) -> caveats (pkg/caveats CEL compile/eval, internal/caveats run across the graph) -> revisions and zedtokens (pkg/zedtoken, pkg/middleware/consistency, internal/datastore/revisions) -> gRPC services internal/services/v1 (permissions, relationships, schema, watch, bulk check, debug traces, reflection). pkg/development + pkg/validationfile run schema + relationships + assertions + expected relations fully in memory. HERMETIC (in-memory datastore memdb or pure logic), measured 2026-11-15 with `go test -tags ci -count=1 -p 2` and --network none, ALL PASS in 252 s: pkg/schema/..., pkg/schemadsl/..., pkg/caveats/..., internal/caveats, pkg/development, pkg/query, pkg/datalayer, pkg/zedtoken, internal/graph/..., internal/dispatch/graph (51 s), internal/dispatch/caching, internal/namespace/..., internal/relationships, internal/services/v1 (28 s; in-process gRPC server over memdb via internal/testserver.NewTestServerWithConfig), internal/services/shared, internal/datastore/memdb (21 s), internal/datastore/proxy/..., pkg/validationfile/.... Test helpers: internal/datastore/dsfortesting.NewMemDBDatastoreForTesting / DataLayerForTesting, internal/testfixtures (standard schemas + relationships), internal/testserver. BUILD TAGS: unit tests run upstream as `-tags ci,memoryprotection -race` (magefiles/test.go); `ci` switches on assertions (pkg/spiceerrors/assert_on.go: internal invariant violations PANIC instead of returning errors) and held-read tracking (pkg/datalayer/heldreads_ci.go), so the verifier must use `-tags ci` (no -race: CGO is off in the image). AVOID everything that needs Docker or a real database: tags `datastore`, `datastore && postgres`, `pgbouncer`, `datastoreconsistency`, `integration`, `steelthread`, `image`, `memoryprotection` test files; packages internal/datastore/{postgres,crdb,mysql,spanner}, internal/testserver/datastore (starts database containers), cmd/spicedb/integration and e2e/ (TestMain + containers), internal/services/integrationtesting/dockertests, internal/fdw e2e, internal/dispatch/combined CA-rotation test, pkg/cache memory-limiter integration test, pkg/testutil/sdbtestcontainer. TestMain: internal/dispatch/graph and internal/taskrunner run goleak.VerifyTestMain (harmless, but a hidden test there that leaves a goroutine running fails the whole package: close every datastore/dispatcher/stream in t.Cleanup); cmd/spicedb/integration and e2e/newenemy have container TestMains (avoid). No AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md in the repo. Measured 2026-11-15 (prototype factory/work/tmp/run6/spicedb-proto/Dockerfile): go mod download 185 s, `go vet -tags ci` of the packages above 195 s, image 4.3 GB, 13.5 min cold including export. TARGET (Sol weaknesses, painpoints.md): PP-17 (first plausible root cause is only one of several places), PP-19/PP-08 (the same permission answer must hold on every path: check, bulk check, lookup resources, lookup subjects, expand, and both evaluators), PP-07 (cached decisions, revisions/zedtokens across calls), PP-03/PP-11 (schema compiler/type system vs evaluation vs API response contracts, caveat context across the graph). Symptoms in API terms only. Hidden tests must be deterministic: no sleeps as synchronization, revision quantization 0 or explicit revisions/zedtokens, no fixed ports (the test server uses bufconn), no shared dirs.
build_rules: Dockerfile: base golang:1.27-bookworm (go.mod needs go >= 1.26.10); git init/fetch the base commit as usual and remove origin; `ENV CGO_ENABLED=0` BEFORE warming (a different value changes the cache key and the verifier would recompile everything); `go mod download` (~3 min); then warm with `go vet -tags ci <packages the task touches and the P2P packages>` and `go test -tags ci -count=1 -run '^$' <same packages>` (links the test binaries; the goleak TestMains are harmless with no tests selected). In the SAME RUN layer finish with `find "$(go env GOCACHE)" -type f -exec touch -m -d '2099-01-01T00:00:00Z' {} +` (intel.md: otherwise Go refreshes cache mtimes and overlayfs copies the cache on every verifier run). Then `ENV GOPROXY=off GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly`. Prototype: factory/work/tmp/run6/spicedb-proto/Dockerfile.
Always pass `-tags ci` (and no other tag) to go vet and go test, in the Dockerfile and in test.sh. Never use -race, `go run mage.go ...`, `go generate`, buf/protoc, or any tag from the AVOID list.

Hidden tests: NEW `*_test.go` files in hermetic packages only (see notes), using only identifiers that exist at base: the in-memory datastore helpers (dsfortesting, memdb, testfixtures), the in-process test server (internal/testserver) with the public v1 gRPC clients, pkg/development / pkg/validationfile entry points, the schema compiler. Avoid type/func names that collide with the package's existing _test.go files (grep first). In internal/dispatch/graph every started dispatcher/datastore must be closed in t.Cleanup (goleak). No new proto fields or regenerated code in the reference fix unless the generated files are committed in the same patch and compile offline.

test.sh: restore every verifier input from the pinned base (all existing *_test.go files in the tested packages, internal/testfixtures, internal/testserver, internal/datastore/dsfortesting, testdata/testconfigs dirs, go.mod, go.sum); delete *_test.go files the base doesn't have in those packages; apply test.patch; then `go test -tags ci -count=1 -v -timeout 10m <pkg> -run '^(exact F2P names)$'`, then the new guards, then NAMED existing tests or whole small packages as PASS_TO_PASS (explicit list; internal/dispatch/graph, internal/services/v1 and internal/datastore/memdb take 20-50 s each, fine as whole packages with `-p 1`); finally `go vet -tags ci` of the touched packages and their dependents. Each group a separate invocation with an expected-pass count check.

Determinism check before finishing: run the F2P + guard groups 5 times in a row on the oracle and once with `-cpu 1,4`; record the result in the build report. Any failure means the test needs explicit sequencing (explicit revisions/zedtokens, at_least_as_fresh or fully_consistent requests, quantization 0), not a retry.
Upstream moves fast: run the AP-6 upstream check on the fix files and search open PRs/issues for the symptom.

surrealdb.name: surrealdb
surrealdb.notes: Rust multi-model database (document + graph), edition 2024, rust-toolchain.toml channel 1.95 (+ wasm32 target, rustfmt, clippy). Root workspace of ~50 crates under surrealdb/: core (the engine: syn = parser front, exec = logical plan + planner + physical operators + permission checks + field rules + live queries, exe, doc = per-record write path incl. events and field/assert processing, idx = indexes, kvs = transactions over the key-value layer, iam = auth/permissions model, catalog = DEFINE'd schema objects, dbs, fnc = functions, lq, cf = change feeds, gql/graphql), parser-next, expr, sqlplan, types, kvs-mem (in-memory store), kvs-surrealkv, rpc, server, pgsql/mysql wire fronts. `language-tests/` is a SEPARATE workspace (own Cargo.lock; excluded from the root) holding the SurrealQL language-test runner `surrealql-test` and 5471 `.surql` test files under language-tests/tests/ (language/statements 1127, reproductions 1194, language/closure 758, language/functions 356, language/planner 153, language/indexes 95, language/write 96, language/graph 63, language/permissions, access/, parsing/ ...). A test file = a `/** ... */` TOML header ([env] namespace/database/auth/imports/timeout/sequential/clean, [test] reason, one [[test.results]] per statement with `value = "..."` or `error = ...`, or a `match` expression) followed by the SurrealQL statements; it runs in-process against the IN-MEMORY engine (default backend `mem`), no server, no network. Run from /app/language-tests: `./target/devopt/surrealql-test run --no-wip <filter>` where the filter is a substring of the path relative to language-tests/tests (one file: `language/statements/define/field/value_reference.surql`; a directory: `language/statements/define/field`). Exit code is non-zero when any test fails. `--results accept` fills in EMPTY results (authoring aid only; read every generated value). Auth-scoped tests set `[env] auth = { level = ... }` or record access via imports; see language-tests/README.md ([env], [test], match expressions) and language-tests/CLAUDE.md. Rust-level tests: `cargo test --locked -p <crate>` in the root workspace (surrealdb/core/tests/*.rs integration tests, unit tests in src), but the ROOT workspace is NOT pre-built in the prototype and compiling surrealdb-core tests is a second 30+ min build: prefer `.surql` hidden tests and use Rust test files only if the behavior cannot be reached from SurrealQL. AVOID: backends other than mem (surrealkv needs a feature build; TiKV/FoundationDB/RocksDB are external), `--endpoint` remote runs, language-tests/tests/upgrade (downloads released binaries), bench/, tests needing [test] requires features that are slow or external, root tests/*_integration.rs (start a server on a port, http/ws/pg/mysql clients), surrealism/wasm extension tests, scripting-heavy tests with tight timeouts, anything using http::* functions or the network. Each test has a DEFAULT 5 s timeout ([env] timeout, ms): under load that flakes, so hidden tests must set `timeout = 30000` (or false) and must not depend on time::now(), rand::*, sleep, generated record ids or unordered SELECT output (use ORDER BY or explicit ids). The repo ships CLAUDE.md (root, language-tests/, surrealdb/core/src/exec/, parser-next) that Codex reads: they describe the test format, a 'Bug Investigation Protocol' and a rule to add reproductions under language-tests/tests/reproductions; check they hold no hint for the chosen defect. MEASURED 2026-11-15 on this host (8 CPUs, 8 GB Docker VM; prototype factory/work/tmp/run6/surrealdb-proto/Dockerfile, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4): toolchain install from rust-toolchain.toml ~3.5 min, `cargo fetch --locked` in language-tests 219 s, cold `cargo build --locked --profile devopt` 34 min with ONE rustc peaking at 7.1 GB RSS, target dir 3.6 GB, image 10.1 GB, export+unpack 11.5 min, total cold image build 64 min. A rebuild after touching surrealdb/core takes 21 min and 7.3 GB (surrealdb-core + the runner crate), so EVERY verifier run and every solver iteration costs ~21 min; `language/statements` (1076 runs) executes in 22 s, define/field (260 runs) in 8 s, all passing offline with --network none; git status stays clean. A no-op `cargo build` in a fresh container recompiled the runner crate (23 min): find and remove the cause before relying on the cached build. TARGET (Sol weaknesses, painpoints.md): PP-18 (state must be right across statements: data, indexes, derived values, later reads, not one query's output), PP-17 (first plausible root cause is one of several places), PP-19/PP-08 (a schema rule or permission must hold on every path that writes or reads the data: CREATE/INSERT/UPSERT/UPDATE/RELATE/DELETE, MERGE/PATCH/CONTENT/SET forms, subqueries, graph traversals, events, live queries, index maintenance), PP-03/PP-11 (parse -> plan -> execute -> result formatting contracts; cases implied by existing language tests), PP-07 (transactions, rollback, events and index state across statements). Because a rebuild is ~21 min, difficulty must come from dependent design decisions, not from the slow loop (AP-9). STATUS 2026-11-15: profile kept but NOT in use; the operator dropped surrealdb for this run because packaging would take 5-7 hours (21-min rebuild per verifier run on an 8 GB host).
build_rules: Dockerfile: base rust:1.95-bookworm; `apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git clang llvm cmake pkg-config libssl-dev protobuf-compiler`; git init/fetch the base commit as usual and remove origin; run `rustc --version` in /app so rustup installs the toolchain named by rust-toolchain.toml while the network is up; `ENV CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`; then in /app/language-tests: `cargo fetch --locked` and `cargo build --locked --profile devopt` (this pre-builds exactly the binary test.sh runs: target/devopt/surrealql-test). If the task also has Rust hidden tests, additionally pre-build ONLY that test target (`cargo test --locked -p <crate> --test <name> --no-run` from /app after `cargo fetch --locked` there); never the whole root workspace. Then `ENV CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true`. target/ is git-ignored; confirm `git status --porcelain` is empty. Start from the prototype factory/work/tmp/run6/surrealdb-proto/Dockerfile and keep its layer prefix byte-identical so the 64-min build comes from cache.

Resources (measured: one rustc peaks at 7.1-7.3 GB; image 10.1 GB; rebuild after a core change 21 min). task.toml: [environment] cpus = 4, memory_mb = 12288, storage_mb = 30720, build_timeout_sec = 7200; [verifier] timeout_sec = 3600; [agent] timeout_sec = 10800. Reasons: 8192 MB leaves under 1 GB above the compiler's peak and an OOM kill looks like a wrong solution; storage must hold the 10 GB image plus a second copy of rebuilt artifacts; the verifier needs one 21-min rebuild plus the test groups; the solver needs several 21-min rebuilds inside its budget.

Long docker steps: the M1 Bash tool kills commands after ~10 min in the background. Build the image from a detached CLI container (intel.md: `docker run -d --name b -v //var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock -v <ctx>:/ctx:ro docker:cli docker build -t <tag> /ctx`, then `docker logs b`) and run every verifier/oracle run as `docker run -d --name X ...` + `docker wait X` + `docker logs X`. Never run two rebuilds at once on this host (8 GB).

Hidden tests: NEW `.surql` files under language-tests/tests/ (e.g. language-tests/tests/language/<area>/<topic>_hidden_<n>.surql), one behavior per file so the log names what failed. Header rules: `[env] timeout = 30000`; explicit record ids; ORDER BY on every multi-row SELECT whose order is not defined; no time::now(), rand::*, sleep::, uuid/ulid generation, http::*, file or network functions; every statement has an explicit [[test.results]] entry (value or error), written by hand from the expected behavior and then confirmed against the reference fix, never accepted blindly from `--results accept`. Each F2P file must FAIL at base on a value/error mismatch, not on a parse error of the test header. New `.rs` test files are allowed only as NEW top-level files `surrealdb/<crate>/tests/<name>.rs` (not under tests/it/, which needs an existing mod.rs edited) using public API that exists at base.

test.sh: restore every verifier input from the pinned base: language-tests/src, language-tests/Cargo.toml, language-tests/Cargo.lock, Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml, .cargo/ if present, and every existing .surql file the P2P groups run (restore the whole language-tests/tests tree from base, then apply test.patch); delete untracked files under language-tests/tests that test.patch did not add. Then `cd /app/language-tests && cargo build --locked --offline --profile devopt` (a compile failure gives reward 0), then `./target/devopt/surrealql-test run --no-wip <filter>` once per group: F2P files, new guard files, then P2P = the existing directories of the touched areas (explicit list, e.g. language/statements/<stmt>, language/permissions, language/indexes). Check the printed `N runs passed` against the expected count for each group so a filter that matches nothing cannot pass.
Existing `.surql` files that pin the base's wrong behavior: test.patch may DELETE them (the gate warns, R1 confirms); never modify them.
Determinism check before finishing: run the F2P + guard groups 5 times in a row on the oracle and once with `--jobs 1`; record the result in the build report.

Upstream check (AP-6) on the fix files, and search language-tests/tests/reproductions at base for an existing reproduction of the same symptom (an existing reproduction file is a hint the solver can grep).
